div.head: Ps Cn for 11
div.ab: Habeantque hii quatuor unam regalem potestatem, salua nobis nostra presentia; quaterque in anno generales foreste demonstrationes et uiridis et ueneris forisfactiones, quas muchimut dicunt, teneant, ubi omnes calumnia[ti] de materia aliqua tangente forestam eant ad triplex iudicium, quod Angli ofgan ꝥ ordel dicunt.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 622 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: And let these four have a royal power, saving to us our presence; and four times a year let them hold general views of the forest and [pleas of] offences of both vert and venison, which they call muchimut (great moot), where all who are accus[ed] in any matter touching the forest shall go to the threefold ordeal, which the English call ofgan ꝥ ordel (to obtain the ordeal).
div.note: In Cn II 30.3; In Cn II 30.3a

königliche Autorität und Competenz auch über Wildfrevel abzuurtheilen hatte im 13. Jh. ein Colleg der Forst-Reiserichter, allerdings öfter vier, das aber nicht in jeder Grafschaft und nicht vierteljährlich, sondern nur nach mehreren Jahren einmal zusammentrat. Vielleicht regte den Verfasser das Reformprogramm für die Periodicität der landrechtlichen Königsrichter-Reisen an, das Magna charta c. 18 ausdrückt: mittemus 2 iusticiarios per unumquemque comitatum per 4 uices in anno, qui cum 4 militibus capiant assisas

Royal authority and competence to judge offences against game as well was held in the 13th century by a body of forest justices in eyre, admittedly often four, which however did not sit in every shire nor quarterly, but only once every several years. Perhaps the author was prompted by the reform programme for the periodicity of the eyres of the royal justices of the general law, which Magna charta c. 18 expresses: mittemus 2 iusticiarios per unumquemque comitatum per 4 uices in anno, qui cum 4 militibus capiant assisas

nach Charta de foresta a. 1217 c. 8 suanimotum teneatur ter in anno; conueniant forestarii, uiridarii, agistatores, aber nicht Forstrichter und nicht zu schwerem Strafgericht, für welches der seit 1189 belegte Name swan-imot, sonst vieldeutig, nicht vorkommt; vgl. Turner p. xxvii ff. Die Form demonstratio freilich lässt Einfluss vermuthen vom uisus nemorum, reguardum, alle drei Jahre; vgl. ebd. p. lxxv

According to Charta de foresta of 1217 c. 8 suanimotum teneatur ter in anno; conueniant forestarii, uiridarii, agistatores, but not forest justices and not for heavy criminal judgement, for which the name swan-imot (attested since 1189, otherwise of many meanings) does not occur; compare Turner p. xxvii ff. The form demonstratio, however, suggests influence from the uisus nemorum, reguardum, every three years; compare ibid. p. lxxv

ofgan hat Ags. Cnut, den Verf. sonst nicht kennt; Hs. H der Inst. hat ofræce. Ersetzt Verf. dies durch ein ihm geläufigeres Wort oder gebraucht er eine mit H gemeinsame, durch ofga glossirte, von H geänderte, Vorlage? Jedenfalls aber irrt Verf., indem er durch Zusammenziehung von 30, 3 und 30, 3a ire und ofgan identificirt und so die Rollen der Gegner verwirrt: er missversteht in 11,1 acquirere als fertig bringen, vollenden, während die Quelle erreichen, erzwingen meint, verkehrt also den Voreid des Klägers zum Ordal des Beklagten

ofgan is in the Old English Cnut, which the author does not otherwise know; MS H of the Inst. has ofræce. Does the author replace this with a word more familiar to him, or does he use an exemplar shared with H, glossed with ofga and altered by H? In any case the author errs in that, by conflating 30, 3 and 30, 3a, he identifies ire and ofgan and so confuses the roles of the opposing parties: in 11,1 he misunderstands acquirere as 'accomplish, complete', whereas the source means 'obtain, compel'; he thus turns the plaintiff's fore-oath into the defendant's ordeal
